product: Q1/What they sell: DKNG is a vertically integrated digital gambling operator - mobile sportsbook live in 27 states + DC + PR (~53% of U.S. population), iGaming in 5 states (~11%) under DraftKings and Golden Nugget Online Gaming brands, DFS in 44 states/DC/Canada, the Jackpocket lottery-courier app, the DraftKings Network media arm, and since Dec-2025 'DraftKings Predictions' CFTC-regulated event contracts (GUS III LLC); the 'Super App' is now live nationwide (Q2-26 8-K/PR, 2026-08-06/07). What a reasonable investor could NOT have known a year ago: that DKNG would be a federally regulated prediction-markets operator whose total revenue is DECLINING (-4.6% y/y in Q2-26 to $1,443M) even as volume grows, and that it would lever up in Aug-2026 ($700M Term Loan B due 2033 + $750M revolver) to retire 0% converts rather than from cash flow. Q4/Suppliers: as the 'only U.S.-based vertically integrated sports betting operator' it has no classic supplier chain - key dependencies are sports data/odds feeds, payment rails, cloud/hosting, and league/media rights (official NBA/MLB/NHL/PGA TOUR/WNBA/NASCAR partner), with no disclosed single-source supplier concentration; the live supplier-adjacent fight is legal, not commercial - on 2026-09-18 DKNG asked the USPTO to void a Cantor Fitzgerald prediction-markets patent (Bloomberg Law).
demand: Q3/Demand is moving with VOLUME and MIX, not price: Q2-26 Sports Consumer Volume rose 14.5% y/y (+$1.67B) to $13.14B and Monthly Unique Payers rose ~9% to 3.6M, while revenue fell 4.6% to $1,443M and ARPMUP fell 13% to $132 - more people betting more money, at a materially lower revenue yield, on a different (promo-loaded, prediction-market) product mix. Q5/Customers: demand is millions of unconcentrated retail bettors, so there is effectively zero customer-concentration risk, but churn/quality risk is worsening rather than improving - sales and marketing jumped 38% y/y to $322.5M and management explicitly blames 'increased promotional reinvestment associated with new customer acquisition'. Q7/Strongest counter-evidence: sports net revenue margin collapsed to 6.8% from 8.7% y/y and Adjusted EBITDA fell 61% to $114.6M in Q2-26, so the bull case needs a margin recovery DKNG has not yet demonstrated, on top of a flat 2026 legal-handle backdrop where growth narratives are concentrating in prediction markets rather than traditional sportsbooks.
pricing_power: Effectively none today: the effective price (net revenue margin / hold) FELL to 6.8% from 8.7% y/y in Q2-26 and ARPMUP fell 13% to $132, with management attributing the drop to customer-friendly sport outcomes and promotional reinvestment - DKNG is giving price away to buy share, not raising it. The partial exceptions are iGaming revenue (+7.5% y/y to $461.9M) and Other revenue (+5.2% to $89.4M), which carry stickier, less promo-sensitive economics than the sportsbook, and event-contract revenue where DKNG can price on its own venue economics. Net: no demonstrated ability to raise price without losing volume in the core sportsbook, and the gross-margin line (-4.1pt y/y, 0.3821) confirms the mix is getting less profitable, not more.
competition: Q6/If DKNG is right, the losers are FanDuel (Flutter), BetMGM, Caesars and ESPN Bet in traditional sportsbook, and most of all the CFTC-regulated prediction-market venues Kalshi and Polymarket plus Robinhood - the 2026-09-13 court ruling that prediction markets are gambling rather than federally regulated trading is a relative win for DKNG/Flutter and a loss for those venues, and DKNG's 2026-09-18 patent petition against Cantor Fitzgerald is the same jurisdictional fight. Q10/Second-and-third-order beneficiaries if the stated trend continues: sports-data/odds and trading-infrastructure vendors, DKNG's bank lenders (Morgan Stanley Senior Funding is administrative agent; the Term Loan B was upsized to $700M on 'strong demand'), Jackpocket's courier/mobile-lottery ecosystem, leagues collecting official-partner fees, and the large-cap index/ETF complexes where DKNG sits - while the DMA/state regulators (Massachusetts, 2026-09-24) are the third-order loser-by-regulation. Q1 angle: what changed in the last 90 days is that DKNG's competitive war shifted from state legislatures to federal courts, and its growth pivot is now explicitly financed with debt.
team: No CEO change - co-founder Jason Robins remains CEO with Matt Kalish and Paul Liberman, and the June-August 8-Ks are signed by Chief Legal Officer/Secretary R. Stanton Dodge. The one dated leadership change is 2026-05-29 (8-K Item 5.02): CFO Alan Ellingson assumed the additional role of principal accounting officer while Erik Bradbury remains Chief Accounting Officer - a controls/reporting-layers tweak, not a strategy shift, but worth watching alongside the accounting-heavy goodwill ($1.60B) and intangible ($837M) balances. Reputational exposure on the marketing/analytics side escalated this week: Massachusetts opened an investigation into gambling companies' use of AI (NYT, 2026-09-24) and the EFF published a companion critique the same day, putting DKNG's growth-marketing leadership in the regulatory spotlight.
market_strategy: Management says it will hold FY26 guidance of $6.5-6.9B revenue and $700-900M Adjusted EBITDA, run the core business toward ~$1B Adjusted EBITDA, and redeploy that flexibility into Predictions to 'win the category this NFL season and beyond' - funded by Aug-2026 debt rather than equity, plus continued buybacks ($154.2M of treasury stock repurchased in 1H26). Q8/If that plays out as described, the next 12 months are a re-rating on Predictions becoming a genuine second growth engine alongside a stabilized sportsbook, with the stock recovering toward sell-side targets - but flag that the programme's own measured finding is that consensus target 'upside' (+58.7% here) is an ANTI-signal (t -3.6 to -7.2 out of sample) and that 27-to-49 dispersion is disagreement, not edge. Q9/If management is wrong in the specific way that Predictions is a low-LTV, promo-fueled margin sink (the thesis behind the ~4% drop on 2026-09-23) and that the 6.8% sportsbook margin is structural rather than sport-outcome-driven, then DKNG has levered up into a decelerating revenue base (-4.6% y/y, -12.3% QoQ), FY26 guidance gets cut, and the equity re-rates toward the low end of the range where a 0.38 gross margin with -4.1pt y/y compression cannot support the multiple.
bull: The one dated tailwind is regulatory, not commercial: a 2026-09-13 court ruling held prediction markets ARE gambling, not federally regulated trading -- a threat to the Kalshi/Polymarket model DraftKings has been losing share to. DraftKings launched its own CFTC-adjacent event-contract product (GUS III) and management is holding its ~$1B EBITDA target into a strong NFL start.
bear: Momentum is negative (21d -12.2%, 63d -14.3%) alongside a declining gross margin (-4.1pp) and a 90-day analyst tally that is net -2 raises, with 2 of the last 3 dated actions being lowers (Citizens 37->35 on 09-24, UBS 49->48 on 09-18). The AGA forecasts a FLAT 2026 legal NFL handle and blames Kalshi/Polymarket for the growth leakage -- this program's own standing finding puts HOOD, not DKNG, on the winning side of that story. Two separate outlets (NYT, EFF) ran stories this week on AI-driven predatory advertising to problem gamblers, and Massachusetts opened an investigation -- a live regulatory/reputational tail. Consensus mean target ($34.86) implies ~59% upside over spot ($21.97), which per SS17 (analyst price-target LEVELS are a measured anti-signal, t -3.6 to -7.2 OOS) is not read as a bullish input.
falsifier: A confirmed Q3 print (expected ~early Nov, unconfirmed) showing handle/EBITDA reacceleration together with the 30-day net-revision count turning positive would falsify the bear case; a third consecutive lowered target or a further gross-margin decline would confirm it.
